subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue with a fixed managed-service heap default now, require a durable --heap-mb/config surface first, or reject daemon heap headroom as the wrong mitigation?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the remaining choice changes managed-service startup defaults and operator tuning behavior, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Land fixed default now
options.body: Accept the proof-sufficient linked PR as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

options.title: Require tuning surface first
options.body: Pause the fix until maintainers choose and test a CLI/config heap-size surface for low-memory hosts and fleet policy.

options.title: Reject heap-headroom mitigation
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide the memory spike must be fixed solely by reducing gateway startup/state memory.

recommendation.title: Land fixed default now
recommendation.body: Accept the proof-sufficient linked PR as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The historical daemon install and host-env security work most directly defines the product/security boundary this choice affects.
